Forts of India: types, famous examples and how to read them

By @archaeologywala for Talaash Heritage · Updated 15 October 2026

India has thousands of forts, built from ancient times to the 19th century: hill forts like Chittorgarh and Kumbhalgarh, desert forts like Jaisalmer, sea forts like Sindhudurg, and city forts like Delhi's Red Fort and Agra Fort. Several are UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including six Hill Forts of Rajasthan and twelve Maratha forts.

Talaash Heritage runs fort walks in Delhi and Haryana and plans forts of Rajasthan journeys for schools, colleges and private groups.

Types of forts in India

Old Indian texts on statecraft, including the Arthashastra and later treatises, classified forts (durga) by the natural defence they used. The categories are still a useful way to understand what you see on the ground.

  • Giri durga, hill forts: built on ridges or flat-topped hills, such as Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Raigad and Gwalior.
  • Jala durga, water forts: protected by sea, river or lake, such as Sindhudurg and Janjira on the Konkan coast, or Gagron in Rajasthan, ringed by two rivers.
  • Dhanvana durga, desert forts: protected by surrounding arid land, such as Jaisalmer.
  • Vana durga, forest forts: protected by dense forest, such as Ranthambore in its jungle setting.
  • Mahi durga, earth or plains forts: with walls of mud, brick or stone on level ground, such as the city walls of Delhi's Tughlaqabad and the Red Fort.

History of forts in India

Fortification in India goes back to the Harappan cities, several of which had massive walls of mud brick or stone. In the early historic period, cities such as Rajgir, Kaushambi and Sisupalgarh had large ramparts and moats. Medieval kingdoms then built hill forts across Rajasthan, central India and the Deccan.

The arrival of gunpowder artillery from the 15th and 16th centuries changed design: walls became thicker and lower, bastions rounder, and gateways were built with sharp turns and spikes against elephants. The Delhi Sultanate and Mughals built city forts as palaces and administrative centres. The Marathas under Shivaji built and rebuilt a network of hill and sea forts in the 17th century. European powers added coastal forts such as Fort St George in Chennai.

Delhi alone has fort walls from many periods. Our walks at Tughlaqabad Fort and Purana Qila show how designs changed between the 14th and 16th centuries.

UNESCO World Heritage forts in India

Forts appear in several of India's 45 World Heritage Sites. Agra Fort was inscribed in 1983 and the Red Fort Complex in 2007. The Hill Forts of Rajasthan, inscribed in 2013, cover six: Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Gagron, Amber and Jaisalmer. The Maratha Military Landscapes of India, inscribed in 2025, cover twelve forts in Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu, including Gingee. Champaner-Pavagadh in Gujarat also includes a fortified hill and city. The full list is in our guide to UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India.

How to read a fort

A site mapping and measured drawing session teaches groups to record these features properly, which is the best way to learn how a fort really works.

  • Gates: count the turns between the outer gate and the palace. Sharp bends slowed attackers and stopped elephants charging.
  • Bastions and walls: round bastions usually mean the builders were thinking about cannon; tall thin walls are often older.
  • Water: every fort needed tanks, wells or cisterns to survive a siege. Find them and you understand how long the fort could hold out.
  • Inscriptions: gateway and temple inscriptions often date a phase of building.
  • Layers: most forts were rebuilt many times. Look for changes in stone, brick and mortar.

Forts of India: notes for students

  • Classical types: hill, water, desert, forest and plains forts.
  • UNESCO forts: Agra Fort (1983), Red Fort Complex (2007), Hill Forts of Rajasthan (2013), Maratha Military Landscapes (2025).
  • Hill Forts of Rajasthan: Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Gagron, Amber, Jaisalmer.
  • Sea forts: Sindhudurg and Janjira on the Konkan coast.
  • Gunpowder changed design from the 15th and 16th centuries: lower, thicker walls and round bastions.

Questions people ask

Which is the largest fort in India?

Chittorgarh in Rajasthan is often called the largest fort in India by area, and Mehrangarh and Gwalior are among the most massive. Kumbhalgarh is famous for one of the longest continuous fort walls in the world. Exact rankings depend on how area and walls are measured.

How many forts in India are UNESCO World Heritage Sites?

Agra Fort and the Red Fort Complex are listed separately, the Hill Forts of Rajasthan group covers six forts, and the Maratha Military Landscapes group covers twelve. Together that is twenty forts within World Heritage listings, plus fortifications at sites such as Champaner-Pavagadh.

Which state has the most forts in India?

Maharashtra is usually said to have the largest number of forts, many of them hill forts linked to the Marathas in the 17th century. Rajasthan is also very rich in forts and is better known for its large palace forts.

What are the types of forts mentioned in ancient Indian texts?

Texts on statecraft group forts by their natural defence: hill forts (giri durga), water forts (jala durga), desert forts (dhanvana durga), forest forts (vana durga) and plains or earth forts. Lists differ slightly between texts.
